reason: The hypothesis relies on a slip-to-twinning transition, but the cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address deformation twinning, strain-rate or temperature effects on twinning in any alloy, nor the Co-free FeNiCrMn system. E1 discusses stacking fault energy and interstitial strengthening in CoCrNi; E2 models precipitation strengthening in CoCrFeMnNi. Neither provides support for the key premises about dynamic deformation mechanisms.
premises: Deformation mechanism in FeNiCrMn transitions from dislocation slip to twinning with increasing strain rate and decreasing temperature.
The absence of Co alters stacking fault energy but the slip-to-twinning transition remains dominant.
High strain rate/low temperature increases twin density, raising yield strength and altering strain hardening.
High temperature/low strain rate promotes dislocation slip, giving lower strength and higher ductility.
The cited evidence supports the slip/twinning transition in related Co-containing alloys.
